title: Concerns Grow Over Conditions on Aircraft Carrier, and Trump Pushes New Hacking Effort
partialText: Plus, your Friday news quiz.

title: Trump’s Justice Dept. Targets Smaller Fraud Cases
partialText: As the Trump administration drops charges against corporations and the wealthy, it is also taking aim at small-scale fraud cases, including against the operator of a weathered food truck in California.

title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Has Been Deployed for Months, Prompting Concerns
partialText: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for nearly nine months. Members of Congress are worried about the crew’s well-being.

title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
partialText: In the tiny nation, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

title: An Unlikely Emergency Appeal to the Supreme Court From a Dog Named Bruce
partialText: A last-ditch filing this week came on behalf of a dog that a judge found to be “vicious” and shows how the court’s emergency docket has been growing.

title: Readers Choose the Best Thrillers and Mysteries of the Century
partialText: The backbone of the list: nine novels by Tana French, and five novels each from John le Carré, Kate Atkinson and Mick Herron.

title: How Thrillers Hook You With Their First Sentence
partialText: Can our Book Review editor, Tina Jordan, guess thrillers from their first sentence? In this game we explore a few of the books from The New York Times’s “50 Best Thrillers of the 21st Century” list; and learn a bit more about why opening sentences are so important to get people reading.

title: Great Movie and TV Adaptations From 21st- Century Thrillers
partialText: From “Slow Horses” to “Big Little Lies,” our list of great psychological thrillers, spy novels and crime fiction have inspired a heap of great adaptations.

title: As Europe Gets Hotter, Its Transportation Systems Struggle to Cope
partialText: The continent’s railways and roads “were engineered for a climate that no longer exists,” one expert said.

title: Heat Is Hammering Europe, Again. Here’s What That Looks Like.
partialText: Extreme temperatures and repeated wildfires are pushing infrastructure to the limit and testing the continent’s resolve.

title: Can Polls Measure the True Strength of the Left?
partialText: Recent polling issues could continue in Democratic primaries in part because progressives are more likely to enjoy taking surveys.

title: Russell Fry Backs Darline Graham in South Carolina Senate Runoff Amid Trump Pressure
partialText: The president has been focused on the race since the death of Lindsey Graham in July. Ms. Graham, the late senator’s sister, is competing against Representative Ralph Norman in a runoff on Aug. 25.

title: Mamdani’s ‘Bro’ Culture in City Hall: Sports, Memes, Nicknames for All
partialText: As much as Zohran Mamdani’s team runs on leftist idealism and social media hits, its style of governing also relies on humor, sports references and pop culture.

title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
partialText: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, a novelty candidate, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

title: Chatbots Are Pushing Us Toward a Post-Human Internet
partialText: In matters of work, school and even romance, we turn to A.I. chatbots. But what happens when the bots begin talking to one another?

title: New Yorkers Can’t Stop Lining Up for This Sushi
partialText: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on sushi and other items are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.

title: Stolen Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse Works Are Recovered, Police Say
partialText: The Italian military police said that art collectively valued at more than $10 million had been found five months after being taken in a nighttime heist near Parma.

title: After Notre-Dame Fire, France Restored the Cathedral — but Not These Windows
partialText: France has faithfully renovated most of what burned at Notre-Dame in 2019. Contentiously, six towering windows will soon be replaced by a new design.

title: 8 Matisse Works, Looted from Library in Brazil, Are Recovered
partialText: The prints by the French master were taken in São Paulo last year in a brazen daylight heist.

title: Is Ocasio-Cortez Ready for the Glass Cliff?
partialText: She will run as a woman but unlike how every woman before her was forced to run.

title: Extreme Heat Is the New Normal
partialText: Firefighters in Phoenix race to save lives in a city that’s only getting hotter.

title: Are Political Polls Accurate?
partialText: We look at recent problems with political polling.

title: Jimmy Fallon Reacts to Karoline Leavitt’s White House Exit
partialText: The “Tonight Show” host said President Trump had been surprised by the press secretary’s decision to step down. “She was like, ‘I wanted to wait for a good time but there hasn’t been one, so.’”

title: Deaths of 3 ICE Detainees Prompt Questions About Medical Care
partialText: Immigrants at Delaney Hall in Newark have complained about health services. Federal officials defended the treatment provided there and elsewhere.
